evals.name: post-merge-cleanup-gt
evals.prompt: Heads up — PR #214 (the bottom of my 3-PR stack on this Graphite repo) just merged into main. What do I run now to get the other two branches caught up and re-submitted? My branches are auth-layer (the one that merged), api-endpoints, and frontend. I'm on the `frontend` branch right now. Walk me through it; don't just hand-wave.
evals.expected_output: Concrete command sequence: gt sync (which fetches trunk, restacks survivors, prompts to delete the merged auth-layer branch), then gt submit --stack to push the rebased survivors. Should NOT recommend bare git rebase or manual base re-targeting. Should mention checking gt log short after.

evals.name: post-merge-cleanup-gh-stack
evals.prompt: The bottom PR in my stack just got merged on GitHub. I'm using the `gh stack` extension. What do I do locally now? Do I have to rebase the rest of the stack myself or did GitHub do it server-side? Be specific about the commands.
evals.expected_output: Should explain that gh stack does server-side cascading rebase at merge time, so the agent's job is to pull state down with `gh stack sync` (not recompute). Should mention `gh stack submit` is only needed if there are unpushed local commits. Should NOT advise bare git rebase. Bonus: mention `gh stack view` to confirm chain.

evals.name: neither-tool-installed
evals.prompt: I want to break this WIP branch into a stacked-PR chain — a couple of small reviewable PRs instead of one big one. Can you set that up? I think I have a fresh repo, nothing fancy installed.
evals.expected_output: Skill should run detection probes (gt --version, gt init marker, gh extension list), find neither is installed, and STOP. Surface the install options for both gt and gh stack with the right install commands. Should NOT improvise with `git checkout -b` + `git push` chains. Should NOT fake stacking with bare git.
